correction_2026_07_27.direction_of_error:
The conclusion survives and strengthens: the orientation was already called
forced, and the true deficit is 48.3 mm rather than 13.5 mm. But the slack was
OVERSTATED (44.94 against 31.85 binding), which is the dangerous direction for a
tolerance figure, and the required mirrored headings were missed entirely.
correction_2026_07_27.guard:
sim/geometry.min_area_rect recovers a rectangle's own axes, and the scorer aims
every placement using it. tests/test_scoring.py asserts that the cable areas are
NOT axis-aligned, so this specific substitution cannot silently return.
correction_2026_07_27.now:
The area is 79.700 x 207.201 mm at 80/100 deg. Slack 39.600 per end along its
long axis, 31.850 per side across, deficit -48.300, and the cable laid at
-10 deg (upper) / +10 deg (lower) in the object frame.
correction_2026_07_27.root_cause:
bbox_mm was read as though it were the area. It is not: for a ROTATED rectangle
the axis-aligned bounding box is strictly larger. 114.47 x 217.89 is the bbox;
the area is 79.700 x 207.201. Every other scoring area happens to be
axis-aligned, so the substitution is invisible on nine of ten areas and wrong on
the tenth.

The data said so and was not read: field_spec records area_mm2 = 16513.822 for
cable_area_upper, against a bounding-box area of 24941.9 mm2 — a 34% gap that
only a rotated shape produces. The roadmap ALSO already recorded the cable area
as 2.5 x 6.5 design units = 79.75 x 207.35 mm, which agrees with the polygon and
contradicts the bbox reading. Two independent records were right and the derived
number was wrong, because it came from a convenience field rather than the
geometry.

cable_orientation.finding:
The cable is 128.0 mm long (2x Technic Brick 1x16). Each grey cable area is a
79.700 x 207.201 mm rectangle — and it is TILTED: cable_area_upper's long axis
lies at 80 deg, cable_area_lower's at 100 deg. They mirror each other about the
horizontal.

128.0 > 79.700, so the cable cannot lie across its area's short axis: it is
48.300 mm too long. The placement orientation is FORCED, and the two cables need
DIFFERENT, mirrored headings — a robot that places both identically gets one
wrong. Worth 30 points (15 per cable, 'completely in the grey area and upright'),
and it constrains the manipulator, not just the strategy: the gripper must be
able to set yaw, and to set it to two different values.

notes: footprint = the CONTACT patch with the mat, not the silhouette. See the module docstring: eight models place a 4x8 plate ON TOP of a 4x4 core, so the plate overhangs at +9.6 mm and is not what touches the mat.
mass_g is null for every object: it cannot be derived from a building instruction. It needs the physical sets on a scale (ADR-014 discipline).
the clef, amp and both speakers score by NOT being moved (S1), so a missing footprint for them blocks no scoring path.

footprint_pending.base_parts: step 88 (p89) places 1x 3001 Brick 2x4 and 2x 3009 Brick 1x6; step 89 (p90) adds 2x more 3009. They form an OPEN rectangular frame, not a filled block.
footprint_pending.bound_note: The isometric fit on page 90 returns 15 stud centres in a 7x7 lattice extent. 7x7 = 56.0 x 56.0 mm is therefore an UPPER BOUND on the base, not a measurement: the extent is real but the count does not verify it, so the true footprint is at most this and probably less.
footprint_pending.why_the_self_check_cannot_apply: The lattice self-check asserts rows*cols == stud count. That holds for a filled rectangle and is false by construction for a frame, whose studs sit only on the perimeter. This is a DIFFERENT failure mode from the note base, which failed on occlusion — here nothing is stacked on the frame at all and the studs are plainly visible. Recording the distinction so the next pass does not retry the occlusion workaround on a problem that is not occlusion.

crosschecks.note:
The 4x8 plate. The inventory says 8; the callout extraction finds cluster 4 on
exactly 8 pages (18, 27, 35, 42, 49, 57, 67, 115) — the second step of the six
notes plus mic and guitar. Two independent counts of the same eight parts.
One flexible hose per cable, and S1 says there are 2 cables.

The cable's rigid carrier. 4 bricks over 2 cables = 2 each, which agrees with
the page-167 callout quantity of 2x. Two per cable placed side by side gives a
2x16 carrier, NOT 1x32 end-to-end — the callout shows a single bar width.

scoring_relevance.note:
S1 scores the clef, the amplifier and the two speakers as 'not damaged or
moved' — 10, 10 and 20 points for LEAVING THEM ALONE. Their footprint is
therefore not on the scorer's containment path at all, and a missing footprint
for the amp or a speaker blocks nothing. This is why part 3 spends its
measurement effort on the cables, keyboard and congas instead.
